steps.title: Power on and Initialize Instrument
steps.instruction: Power on the MiSeq and allow the software to load.

substeps.instruction: Flip the power switch on the back of the instrument.
Enter username and password if the instrument is networked.
Wait for the MiSeq Control Software (MCS) to load and complete initialization.

steps.title: Prepare Reagent Cartridge
steps.instruction: Thaw and prepare the reagent cartridge and HT1.

substeps.instruction: Thaw the cartridge and HT1 on ice or at 2-8°C.
Invert the thawed reagent cartridge 10 times to mix.
Visually inspect to ensure reagents are completely thawed and free of precipitates.
Gently tap the cartridge on the bench to dislodge air bubbles from the bottom of the wells.
Wipe the cartridge with a paper towel.
Store the thawed cartridge and HT1 on ice or at 2-8°C in the dark until loading.

steps.title: Verify Disk Space
steps.instruction: Ensure the instrument has at least 100GB of free disk space on the D:\ drive.

substeps.instruction: If space is insufficient, navigate to D:/Illumina/MiSeqOutput/(most recent run folder) and delete the 'Images' and 'Thumbnail_images' folders.
Navigate to D:/Illumina/MiSeqAnalysis/ and delete all run folders except the most recent one.
Reboot the instrument after deletion to free virtual memory.

steps.title: Configure Run Setup
steps.instruction: Set up the run parameters in the MCS.

substeps.instruction: Select a run option: 'Local Run Manager' (for pre-set runs), 'Sample Sheet' (for generated sample sheets), or 'Manual' (no secondary analysis).
Enter BaseSpace email and password if applicable, then select Next.
Select the specific Local Run Manager run or sample sheet based on the previous choice.

steps.title: Prepare and Load Flow Cell
steps.instruction: Clean and install the flow cell from Box 2 of 2 (stored at 2-8°C).

substeps.instruction: Wearing clean, powder-free gloves, remove the flow cell by gripping the plastic end.
Lightly rinse both sides of the glass and plastic casing with molecular-grade water to remove salts.
Pat dry with a lint-free wipe, avoiding the black port gasket.
Clean the glass portion with lens paper wetted with ethanol (or an alcohol wipe); do not add ethanol directly to the flow cell or gasket.
Dry excess ethanol with lens paper and inspect for smudges, debris, and the seating of the port gasket.
Open the flow cell compartment door, press the release button to remove the old flow cell, and place the new flow cell on the stage by its edges.
Press down the flow cell clamp until it clicks and close the door.

steps.title: Load PR2 and Waste Bottles
steps.instruction: Prepare the fluidic bottles in the reagent compartment.

substeps.instruction: Gently invert the PR2 bottle to mix and remove the lid.
Open the reagent compartment door and raise the sipper handle until it locks.
Remove the wash bottle and load the PR2 bottle; re-cap the wash bottle for future use.
Empty the waste bottle into an appropriate chemical waste container.
Lower the sipper handle, ensuring it enters the PR2 and waste bottles.

steps.title: Load Sample into Cartridge
steps.instruction: Add the denatured DNA library to the reagent cartridge.

substeps.instruction: Remove the thawed reagent cartridge, ensuring it is dry and mixed.
Tap the cartridge on a hard surface to collect contents at the bottom.
Pierce the foil seal of the 'Load Sample' reservoir using a clean 1000 μl pipette tip.
Transfer 600 µL of denatured DNA library into the reservoir, avoiding droplets on the foil seal.
Tap the cartridge gently on the tabletop to remove any bubbles from the bottom of the reservoirs.

steps.title: Install Reagent Cartridge
steps.instruction: Place the loaded cartridge into the chiller.

substeps.instruction: Verify the MCS screen states 'Load Reagent Cartridge'.
Open the reagent chiller door, remove the wash tray, and dry the bottom of the compartment if necessary.
Slide the reagent cartridge (holding by the Illumina label end) into the chiller until it stops.
Close the chiller door and confirm the software identifies the cartridge RFID.
Close the reagent compartment door.

steps.title: Start Sequencing Run
steps.instruction: Perform final checks and initiate the run.

substeps.instruction: Select Next, review run parameters, and select Next to start the Pre-Run Check.
Once the pre-run check passes, select 'Start Run'.
Do not open the instrument or touch the monitor during the run to avoid vibration.

steps.title: Perform Post-Run Bleach Wash
steps.instruction: Clean the system after a run to reduce nucleic acid carryover.

substeps.instruction: Select 'Start Wash' in the MCS and check 'Perform optional template line wash'.
Prepare 0.5% Tween-20 Wash: Add 25 µL of 10% Tween-20 (5 µL Tween-20 in 45 µL water) to 475 µL molecular-grade water.
Prepare 0.01% NaOCl: Mix 36 µL of 5% NaOCl with 864 µL water (0.2% NaOCl), then add 50 µL of this 0.2% NaOCl to 950 µL water. Add the entire 1.0 mL to a wash tube.
Insert the 0.01% NaOCl tube into position 17 of the wash tray only.
Add at least 6 µL of 0.5% Tween-20 to all other wash tray reservoirs and 350 µL to the 500 ml wash bottle.
Open the reagent compartment and chiller doors; remove the used cartridge.
Slide the wash tray into the chiller and close the door.
Raise the sipper handle, replace the PR2 bottle with the wash bottle, and empty the waste bottle into a formamide-appropriate container.
Lower the sipper handle and close the reagent compartment door.
Select 'Done' after the wash is complete; leave the flow cell, tray, and bottle on the instrument.

steps.title: Perform Maintenance or Standby Washes
steps.instruction: Maintain the instrument during idle periods or every 30 days.

substeps.instruction: For Post-Run/Weekly Wash: Select 'Perform Wash' -> 'Perform Post-Run Wash' with a loaded flow cell and fresh 0.5% Tween-20 (6 µL per reservoir, 350 µL in bottle).

For Maintenance Wash (every 30 days): Select 'Perform Wash' -> 'Perform Maintenance Wash'. Use fresh 0.5% Tween-20. When prompted, replace the first wash tray/bottle with a second fresh set, then replace the second with a refilled first set.
For Standby Wash (>14 days idle): Perform two 60-minute washes with 0.5% Tween-20. Repeat every 30 days. Perform a maintenance wash to bring the instrument out of idle mode.

steps.title: Weekly System Reboot
steps.instruction: Reboot the system weekly or after file deletion.

substeps.instruction: Select 'Manage Instrument' then 'Reboot' (approx. 10 mins).
Alternatively, select 'Shut Down', flip the power switch on the back, wait 1 minute, and power back on.

steps.title: Prepare Denatured PhiX Library
steps.instruction: Prepare PhiX control for 20 pM (v3 chemistry) or 12.5 pM (v2 chemistry).

substeps.instruction: Prepare 0.2 N NaOH and keep on ice.
Combine 2 µL of 10 nM PhiX stock and 3 µL of EBT to get 4 nM PhiX.
Combine 5 µL of 4 nM PhiX and 5 µL of 0.2 N NaOH; mix well.
Incubate for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Immediately add 990 µL of pre-chilled HT1 to obtain 20 pM denatured PhiX.
For v2 chemistry: Remove 375 μl from the 20 pM dilution and add 375 μl of HT1 to reach 12.5 pM.

steps.title: Spike PhiX into Sample Library
steps.instruction: Add PhiX to the final denatured sample library.

substeps.instruction: Dilute 20 pM PhiX to 8 pM by adding 40 µL library to 60 µL pre-chilled HT1.
For a 1% spike: Add 10 μl of 8 pM PhiX to 990 μl of sample library.
For other percentages (N%): Combine N x 10 μl of 8 pM PhiX with (1000 – (N x 10)) μl of sample library.

steps.title: Export Sample Sheet
steps.instruction: Generate and transfer the .csv sample sheet from the workbook.

substeps.instruction: Populate the SampleSheet tab (do not modify Indices tab).
Save or Export the active sheet as a .csv (Comma delimited) using the Plate ID as the filename.
Transfer the file to the MiSeq Sample Sheet folder or shared network drive.

Enter required fields: Run Name, Library Prep Kit (Nextera XT or DNA CD Indexes), Indexes (96 Indexes Plated), Read Type (Paired End), Read Length (151 or 251 for R1 and R2), and Adapter Trimming (ON).
Enter the number of rows, ensuring Sample ID and Index Well are provided.
